name: import_document
description: Ingest an on-disk Markdown file into the OPEN session (the file-ingress half compose_document lacks: compose takes an inline string only). Reads the file under the workspace jail, then runs the identical compose pipeline (strict compile gate, quotas, template-seed check, inline-span splitting), so the result is byte-equal to composing the same Markdown inline. sessionId is strictly required: the tool never auto-creates sessions (fresh templated document: new_document first, then import; existing file: open_document first, then import). Accepts .md/.markdown/.txt; .html/.htm refuse with E_VALIDATION (convert to Markdown first, same verdict as CLI import); .docx refuses with E_VALIDATION naming open_document (open .docx files directly). Outside-jail reads fail E_SANDBOX, missing files E_IO, oversize files E_LIMIT. Optional allowedDir (image refs), template (report|memo|blank seed check), and styleGuide (same attach semantics as compose_document). Optional dollarMath (default false) treats $...$ as inline math; off by default because prices and shell text can look like math. Example {"sessionId":"sess_abc","path":"documents/notes.md"} -> compose envelope. IDs are session-scoped: valid only in the issuing session, must not be stored across sessions. ECMA-376 essentials: colors are hex without # (e.g. 4F46E5, never #4F46E5); font sizes are half-points in w:sz (e.g. 28 = 14pt, 22 = 11pt); spacing/margins/cellMar use twips dxa (twentieths of a point, e.g. 240 = 12pt, 180 = 9pt); borders use eighths-of-a-point sz (e.g. 32 = 4pt left accent). Workflow: open_document -> inspect_document -> search_content -> execute_batch -> save_document -> close_document. Always inspect first, batch second, save third. Single edit = 1-item batch. Never call twice when once suffices.
